| Part | Runs on | Does |
|---|---|---|
| Web app | Next.js 16 on Vercel | The landing page, sign-in, the dashboard, public scans and reports, run pages, the change catalog, these docs, and the GitHub webhook endpoint |
| Worker | Node 24 on Coolify | Webhooks, scans, fix runs, commands, the Dashboard issue, and the reliability ticker |
| Postgres | Coolify | Findings, runs, events, receipts, the catalog, sessions, the outbox, and the job queues |
| Sandbox | Cloudflare Containers | Installs and checks, one isolated container per side of a run |
| Models | Nebius Token Factory | NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, with Super as failover |
| Search | Tavily | Finding the notices of a provider that has no reader |

## From GitHub to the worker

<Steps>
<Step>

`POST /api/github/webhooks` checks the `X-Hub-Signature-256` signature. It stores the delivery once, keyed by GitHub's delivery ID, so a redelivery is a no-op. It wakes the worker with `pg_notify`, then answers **202**.

</Step>
<Step>

The worker listens for that notification and also polls every 5 seconds. It claims up to 10 deliveries at a time (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`). A claim older than 5 minutes is taken again, and a delivery that fails 5 times is set aside with its error.

</Step>
<Step>

Scans and fix runs go onto pg-boss queues in the same database. Each queue runs one job at a time per repository, in order, so two scans or two fix runs never race on one repository. Handlers never throw: a failure is stored on the scan or run, and the next job proceeds.

</Step>
</Steps>

The web app's own requests travel the same outbox as synthetic events: public scans, dry runs and the dashboard's buttons. So the web app never calls the worker directly.

## Reliability

A ticker runs every 60 seconds. It:

- writes the worker's heartbeat,
- fails runs whose heartbeat stopped for 10 minutes (runs beat every 15 seconds) and scans running over 45 minutes,
- publishes which models are healthy,
- re-checks Token Factory credits every 15 minutes,
- starts scheduled rescans (`schedule: daily | weekly`),
- every 10 minutes, asks GitHub for failed webhook deliveries from the last 6 hours and redelivers the ones it never stored.

The [trust page](/trust) shows all of it live.

## Public endpoints

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/catalog/changes` | Every public, confirmed change, filterable by `provider`, `ecosystem`, `kind` and `subject` |
| `GET /api/catalog/changes/<id>` | One change record |
| `GET /api/catalog/providers` | Every provider Teire can read, with its pages and SDKs |
| `GET /api/runs/<id>/sheet?after=<seq>` | A run as its page shows it (status, evidence, checks, receipts) with the events after `seq`: the feed behind the live run page. Public repositories' runs are open to anyone; private ones to people with access to the installation |
| `GET /schema.json` | The JSON Schema of `teire.yml` |
| `GET /llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` | These docs as plain text for language models |

The CLI reads the catalog endpoints; they need no key.

## Source

[github.com/teire-dev/teire](https://github.com/teire-dev/teire) is a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo:

<Files>
  <Folder name="apps" defaultOpen>
    <Folder name="web" />
    <Folder name="worker" />
    <Folder name="sandbox" />
  </Folder>
  <Folder name="packages" defaultOpen>
    <Folder name="engine" />
    <Folder name="db" />
    <Folder name="cli" />
    <Folder name="helpers" />
  </Folder>
</Files>

The engine holds everything that reads, diffs, locates, fixes and verifies. The worker, the CLI and the MCP server all call it the same way.
